subject: Maths
title: Transformations of graphs
subtitle: Functions and Graphs · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can describe and apply translations, reflections and stretches to graphs of functions.

key_vocab.term: A transformation changes the position or shape of a graph. Key types

key_vocab.definition: f(x) + a shifts up, f(x + a) shifts left, -f(x) reflects in x-axis, f(-x) reflects in y-axis.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can describe and apply translations, reflections and stretches to graphs of functions.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content:
A transformation changes the position or shape of a graph. Key types -- translations (shifts), reflections (flips), and stretches (scaling).
Notation -- f(x) + a shifts up, f(x + a) shifts left, -f(x) reflects in x-axis, f(-x) reflects in y-axis.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Changes inside the bracket affect x (horizontal, opposite direction). Changes outside affect y (vertical, same direction).
y = af(x + b) + c
a = vertical stretch, b = horizontal shift (opposite), c = vertical shift

Key examples:
  ✓ f(x) + 3 shifts the graph up 3  (vertical translation)
  ✓ f(x - 2) shifts the graph right 2  (horizontal translation)
  ✓ -f(x) reflects in the x-axis  (y-values change sign)
  ✗ f(x + 2) shifts the graph right 2  (it shifts LEFT 2)
  ✗ f(x) + 3 shifts the graph right 3  (it shifts UP 3)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – vertical translation
  Describe the transformation from y = x² to y = x² + 5
  Compare: f(x) = x² and f(x) + 5
  The +5 is outside: vertical shift
  Translation 5 units up
  Translation by vector (0, 5)
  (Adding outside the function shifts the graph up.)

Example 2 – horizontal translation
  Describe the transformation from y = x² to y = (x - 3)²
  Compare: f(x) = x² and f(x - 3)
  The -3 is inside: horizontal shift
  Opposite direction: shift right 3
  Translation by vector (3, 0)
  (Inside the bracket, the shift is in the opposite direction.)

sections.title: Vertical translations
sections.content:
Describe each transformation from y = f(x).

(a) y = f(x) + 4
(b) y = f(x) - 2
(c) y = x² + 7 from y = x²
(d) y = x³ - 1 from y = x³

sections.title: Horizontal translations
sections.content:
Describe each transformation from y = f(x).

(a) y = f(x - 5)
(b) y = f(x + 3)
(c) y = (x - 1)² from y = x²
(d) y = (x + 4)³ from y = x³

sections.title: Reflections
sections.content:
Describe each transformation.

(a) y = -f(x)
(b) y = f(-x)
(c) y = -x² from y = x²
(d) y = (-x)³ from y = x³

sections.title: Stretches
sections.content:
Describe the stretch.

(a) y = 2f(x)
(b) y = f(3x)
(c) y = 5 sin x from y = sin x
(d) y = cos(2x) from y = cos x

sections.title: Mixed transformations
sections.content:
Describe the transformation from y = f(x).

(a) y = f(x + 2) + 3
(b) y = -f(x) + 1
(c) y = 2f(x - 4)
(d) y = f(2x) - 5
(e) y = -f(x - 1) + 2

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ f(x + 2) shifts the graph left 2
✗ f(x + 2) shifts the graph right 2
✓ -f(x) reflects the graph in the x-axis
✗ f(x) + 3 shifts the graph right 3
✓ 2f(x) stretches the graph vertically by factor 2

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Vertical translations:
  (a) Translation (0, 4) up
  (b) Translation (0, -2) down
  (c) Translation 7 up
  (d) Translation 1 down

Horizontal translations:
  (a) Translation (5, 0) right
  (b) Translation (-3, 0) left
  (c) Translation 1 right
  (d) Translation 4 left

Reflections:
  (a) Reflection in x-axis
  (b) Reflection in y-axis
  (c) Reflection in x-axis
  (d) Reflection in y-axis

Stretches:
  (a) Vertical stretch SF 2
  (b) Horizontal stretch SF &frac{1}{3}
  (c) Vertical stretch SF 5
  (d) Horizontal stretch SF &frac{1}{2}

Mixed transformations:
  (a) Left 2, up 3
  (b) Reflect in x-axis, then up 1
  (c) Right 4, vertical stretch SF 2
  (d) Horizontal stretch SF &frac{1}{2}, down 5
  (e) Right 1, reflect in x-axis, up 2
